prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut demi statue portrait, a fine horizontal-striped crystal-and-wood body, every material seam physically stepped. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh-stub tips just below her hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Japanese woman in ko-gyaru makeup — deeply sun-tanned bronze makeup over real skin, bold white eyeshadow across the lids, white glossy lips, a bright turquoise liner accent at the outer corners, long lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, long bleached blonde hair with sun-streaked highlights, a bright cheeky grin. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a huge thick gold hoop hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulder.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, her body finely striped crystal and wood, each stripe physically stepped from the next.

Boundary (skin to material, at the collarbones): a single straight, flat line runs around the base of her neck and across both collarbones, nowhere lower, never reaching her chest — never jagged, never zigzag, a clean straight cut like a cross-section. Real skin above this straight line, the material immediately below it. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow.

Her whole body below the collarbones is patterned in narrow horizontal stripes, each about two finger-widths tall, alternating evenly between solid transparent crystal (solid golden-yellow citrine crystal, with faint feathery inclusions and colour zoning, deep honey-gold where thickest and pale lemon at every thin edge) and carved dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, the stripes running unbroken across her shoulders, chest, belly, hips and both thigh-stubs. At every seam where two different materials meet, one material's edge rises very slightly above its neighbour, catching a thin, crisp shadow line — this tiny physical step, repeated at every single boundary in this pattern, is what proves each piece is a truly separate object, not a flat pattern painted onto one continuous surface.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a warm golden amber on one side and a deep charcoal grey on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (crystal) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so amber light glances off one side and grey light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint of shadow along every stepped seam, light passing straight through every crystal stripe while only reflecting off every wood stripe. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
